method: Read-only audit. Every count was produced by decompressing and parsing the real files on disk (gzcat|wc -l, python json parsing) or by re-executing the Arena loader arena.environments.formal_structural.load_formal_states with PYTHONPATH=. . No Lean, lake or mathlib build was run; no model/LLM call was made; nothing outside the Arena parallel worktree was written. Tactic text was recovered offline by slicing the byte range action.source_location.start.raw..end.raw out of the pinned local mathlib/Batteries source file named by corpus_metadata.source_file.

caveats: Tier A applies to the STATES only. The structural answer (which identifier is deepest) is Tier B: Arena recomputes it. Nothing in the record certifies that the tactic step was replayed.

Goal-management combinators are hugely over-represented relative to the LeanDojo reference: exacts 88/1150 = 7.7% (vs ~0.1% in LeanDojo val+test), all_goals 51 = 4.4%, swap 39 = 3.4%, case 18, on_goal 11. Any 'which reasoning operation' claim built on this corpus must be reweighted or drawn from LeanDojo instead.

candidate_task_families.distractors: REAL, not invented. Four ready sources, in increasing hardness: (1) uniform draw from the 180,973-declaration corpus; (2) same-file declarations (corpus.jsonl groups by path); (3) same-namespace / shared name prefix; (4) HARD - premises cited at OTHER steps of the SAME theorem, which are all genuinely relevant to the proof but wrong here.
shortcut_leak_risks: LEXICAL OVERLAP: the correct premise name usually shares tokens with the goal (e.g. goal mentions Finset.sum_Ico, answer is Finset.sum_Ico_eq_sub). A pure string-overlap baseline must be measured FIRST and distractors matched on overlap, or the mechanism measures string matching.
FREQUENCY PRIOR: the head of the premise distribution is extremely skewed (rfl 140, Max.max 81, mul_assoc 71 in val+test alone). Frequency-match the distractors.
MEMORISATION: mathlib @29dcec07 (2024-07) is public. Use the novel_premises split and the obfuscation arm.
PROOF-POSITION: proof_depth/proof_length are available in lean_pipeline_v1 and correlate with premise class.

obfuscation_arm_feasibility.verdict: FEASIBLE AND STRUCTURALLY SUPPORTED for the STRUCTURED corpus; NOT cleanly feasible for the pretty-printed LeanDojo text.
obfuscation_arm_feasibility.why_structured_works: transcribe() puts each symbol's name in CanonicalExpression.value with the tree shape held separately in .args. A per-item salted bijection over the 2,240 distinct symbol names (and the sort-level parameter names and local_instances.class_identity) rewrites value fields only. Tree shape, node count, depth, arity, binder roles, de Bruijn indices and the token multiset are all invariant, so EVERY structural answer is preserved by construction. arena/environments/formal_structural.relabel() already implements exactly this discipline for local references and is the template.
obfuscation_arm_feasibility.why_text_is_harder: Renaming inside rendered Lean syntax has to survive notation, unicode operators, coercion arrows and implicit-argument elision without changing what the state MEANS. Doing it soundly amounts to re-pretty-printing from the elaborated term, i.e. re-running Lean.
obfuscation_arm_feasibility.recommended_design: Three arms on the same items: REAL names / CONSISTENT-BIJECTION names / SHUFFLED-INCONSISTENT names. A drop from arm 1 to arm 2 measures name-recall; a drop from arm 2 to arm 3 measures whether the model is using name consistency at all.

non_memorisation_leaks_measured_here.note: Recomputed directly from the 461 eligible / 104 length-fair states. These are STRUCTURAL leaks, not memorisation, and they are WORSE than the figure published in docs/FITNESS_V5_SPEC.md.

non_memorisation_leaks_measured_here.consequence: In the shallow stratum the first-mentioned rule is correct 34/34 times. A shortcut-clean formal_expression_depth instrument cannot be built from these states by filtering alone; option ordering, first-mention balancing and a frequency control are all required, and even then the residual is large. This corroborates and strengthens the existing 'do not reuse formal_expression_depth as-is' warning.
